title: Sparsity of the constructed threshold parity target
statement: Let $m\ge 7$, and define a Boolean function on $2^m$ signs by taking the product over $b=0,\ldots,m-1$ of the signs encoding the mod-two inner products of the two length-$m$ blocks selected from coordinates indexed by $b$ in the first and second halves of the coordinate range. If a real-valued function on this sign cube represents the target by threshold signs, then it has at least $2^{m^2}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients.
hypotheses_covered: the real-valued function is defined on the sign cube of dimension $2^m$
it represents the constructed target by threshold signs
caveat: The target's coordinate-selection rule is intricate; the description summarizes its block-indexing construction.
